source.title: Ax-Schanuel for Shimura varieties
source.authors: Ngaiming Mok, Jonathan Pila, Jacob Tsimerman
readSections: Entire published article, pp. 945-978, including all three parts and references; extracted text.
Published page images 959, 965, 969, 971 and 974 checked for selected formulas/interfaces.
arXiv v3 p. 23 compared for Theorem 11.3 only; not a full version comparison.

summary: Source extraction of pure, jet and differential Ax-Schanuel, with the definable Hilbert-family proof, domain rigidity, Schwarzians and differential-field interfaces split into individual obligations. Five pinned library imports are reused. Two extensions provide domain jet rigidity and the independent functional-transcendence supplier; existing owners retain jets, Hilbert schemes, analytic spaces and counting. Four generic monodromy/quotient prerequisites remain unrouted, and precise source/compatibility gaps prevent a complete claim.

items.name: Definable Remmert-Stein extension
items.statement: Let M be a definable complex manifold, E a definable complex analytic subset of M, and A a definable complex analytic subset of M minus E. Then the closure of A in M is complex analytic. Definability removes the dimension restriction of the classical Remmert-Stein statement.

items.name: Definable Chow algebraization
items.statement: A closed complex analytic subset of a complex quasi-projective algebraic variety which is definable in an o-minimal expansion of the real field is algebraic. Closedness is relative to the algebraic ambient variety.

items.name: Projective Chow theorem
items.statement: Closed analytic subspaces of complex projective space are algebraic with their coherent ideals. This general supplier is distinct from definable algebraization on a nonproper open variety.

items.name: Algebraization after arithmetic descent
items.statement: If A in Omega times X is closed analytic, Gamma-invariant on the first factor, and A intersect (F times X) is definable, then (q times id)(A) is closed algebraic in X times X. The covering quotient supplies local analytic descent; definable Chow supplies algebraicity.

The printed Corollary 3.2 also says closed; retain that hypothesis for a literal invocation and prove the intended constructible version separately.
items.note: Closed appears in the published statement despite the subsequent constructible applications. This extraction does not silently drop the word or use an arbitrary nonproper analytic image as a constructible set.

items.name: Connected algebraic monodromy normality
items.statement: For the polarizable rational variation in use over a smooth connected algebraic base, the identity component of algebraic monodromy is normal in the derived generic Mumford-Tate group. State the chosen connectedness and generic-point hypotheses from Andre section 5.
items.locator: Section 4 cites Deligne and Andre 1992 section 5
items.note: Original Andre scan acquired but not read successfully; its exact primary theorem and proof leaves remain open. This conditional contract is not a completed general Hodge-theory extraction.

items.name: Dense monodromy at weakly special generic image
items.statement: For the algebraic image in the proof which is not contained in a proper weakly special locus, obtain Zariski-dense monodromy in the effective semisimple G. This needs the weakly special closure/monodromy comparison, not merely generic Mumford-Tate generality.

items.name: Finite-index monodromy of the incidence component
items.statement: Over a suitable dense smooth open of its algebraic image, a proper dominant incidence component with finitely many fibre components induces finite-index monodromy. Use the descended incidence quotient and a connected component, not the fundamental group of an unrelated simply connected lift.
items.note: The printed notation for pi_1(A prime) requires reconciliation with descent; the generic connected-fibre/finite-component topological argument is not yet source-closed.

items.name: Normality of the generic stabilizer closure
items.statement: In the counterexample induction of section 4, Theta is normal in G: very general arithmetic stabilizers are conjugated along the algebraic family, and the finite-index dense monodromy subgroup normalizes their connected Zariski closure.

items.name: Normal factors of the domain
items.statement: For a connected normal semisimple subgroup Theta of effective G, obtain the complementary normal factor and product decomposition of the Hermitian domain, with arithmetic quotient/product comparison after finite covers. Quotients and finite kernels remain explicit.

items.name: Triviality from induction on the domain and defect
items.statement: In a minimal counterexample, Theta invariance and the product factor projection would give a smaller-domain counterexample; compare dimensions of W and U in the projected factors to conclude Theta is trivial.

items.name: Exponential volume growth in a Hermitian domain
items.statement: A positive-dimensional closed complex analytic subvariety of the bounded symmetric domain has volume in large invariant-metric balls bounded below by c exp(a R), with positive constants allowed to depend on the subvariety and basepoint. Use the exact dimensional Hwang-To version required in section 4.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3; KUY Theorem 5.7 quotes the curve case
items.note: KUY pp. 349-351 read only establish the quoted curve version. General-dimensional input and original Hwang-To proof remain explicit source gaps.

items.name: Uniform fundamental-set volume for algebraic curves
items.statement: There is A depending on the fixed domain and Siegel fundamental set such that Vol(C intersect F)<=A deg C for any algebraic curve C in the domain, in the fixed embedding. KUY proves this from Mumford metric comparison and coordinate projections of degree at most deg C.

items.name: Uniform volume for the definable analytic family
items.statement: Obtain a common bound for volumes of the translated analytic members on F used in Lemma 4.3. On complex d-dimensional rank strata expand omega^d, use generic finite coordinate projections and uniform definable fibre cardinality; lower-rank strata contribute no top-dimensional measure.
items.locator: Main Lemma 4.3, adaptation of KUY Lemma 5.8
items.note: This adaptation is not supplied by the algebraic-curve statement alone; real dimension 2d must not be used as the complex wedge exponent. Measure/change-of-variables and metric comparison proof leaves remain open.

items.name: Definable set of large-intersection translates
items.statement: Let I consist of g in G(R) for which gW meets D inside F times X in the prescribed real dimension 2 dim_C U. Prove definability from uniformization on F and definable fibre dimension; use inverse representatives when U meets gamma F.

uses.how: Turn large graph intersections into a definable family with arithmetic points.

items.name: Polynomially many bounded-height translates
items.statement: Volume growth, the uniform volume upper bound and the distance-height comparison yield at least c T^delta arithmetic points in the appropriate definable translate set for arbitrarily large T. Constants are fixed for the chosen counterexample.

items.name: Pila-Wilkie counting outside the algebraic part
items.statement: For every epsilon>0 a definable set has O(T^epsilon) rational points of height at most T outside the union of its positive-dimensional connected semialgebraic subsets. Family uniformity/block refinements must be stated separately when used.

items.name: A semialgebraic curve with two arithmetic points
items.statement: Use the appropriate uniform/block counting refinement to find one connected real semialgebraic curve in I containing at least two distinct arithmetic points; polynomial growth alone and the bare algebraic-part definition do not prove this without a finite-complexity bound.
items.note: Exact counting refinement and original proof locator remain to acquire; retain as a specific prerequisite, not a falsely immediate corollary.

items.name: Translate-family intersection and union induction
items.statement: For the complexification C of the semialgebraic curve, compare W_c: if locally constant, two distinct arithmetic translates give a nonidentity stabilizer; otherwise use either a generic pairwise intersection lowering defect or the algebraic union increasing dim U while keeping the required defect. Check analytic components and generic dimension at each branch.

items.name: Infinite arithmetic stabilizer of a minimal counterexample
items.statement: The translate induction produces a nontrivial arithmetic stabilizer; torsion-freeness gives infinite order. This contradicts Theta triviality because an infinite subgroup has positive-dimensional algebraic closure in characteristic zero.

items.name: Ax-Schanuel for the pure uniformization graph
items.statement: Let W=W_hat intersect (Omega times X), with W_hat irreducible algebraic in OmegaHat times X. If U is an irreducible analytic component of W intersect D and dim_C W<dim_C U+n, then the X-projection of U is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety. Mixed exponential uniformization is not an instance of this theorem.

items.name: Two-sorted Ax-Schanuel inequality
items.statement: For irreducible complex analytic Y in Omega, dim Y_Zar+dim q(Y)_Zar >= dim Y+dim Y_WS, with algebraic closures taken in the compact-dual/domain and X conventions and Y_WS the smallest weakly special domain locus.

items.statement: D_k^r=Spec C[epsilon_1,...,epsilon_r]/(epsilon_1,...,epsilon_r)^(k+1), using total degree, not separate truncation of each variable. It has a distinguished origin and truncation maps.

items.statement: An order-k equation on maps into X is an algebraic subvariety W of J_k^r X; a map solves it when its actual k-jet takes values in W. Formal points of W need not integrate to solutions.

items.statement: J_k^r q is an analytic Gamma covering onto J_k^r X. Over the preimage of F it is definable because derivatives of a definable holomorphic map are definable and jet composition is polynomial in those derivatives and input coefficients.

items.statement: The effective G(C) acts freely on id_2(o), hence on J_k^(nd,r) OmegaHat for k>=2 and r>=n. Reduce a possible negative-root stabilizer to the fractional-linear rank-one calculation. An ineffective group such as Sp with central minus identity is not literally free.

items.statement: Establish that W_k is closed in the nondegenerate locus for k>=2 and that W_3 to W_2 is an isomorphism on the required charts. Freeness alone does not prove closedness of arbitrary algebraic group orbits; supply the homogeneous-orbit argument and separability.

items.statement: For a holomorphic f with a=f prime nonzero, b=f double-prime and c=f triple-prime, S(f)=c/a-(3/2)(b/a)^2. In Taylor coordinates f(z+t)=f(z)+at+bt^2/2+ct^3/6, the normalized cubic coefficient is S(f)/6.

items.name: Order-three local rigidity
items.statement: If a local biholomorphism F on the compact-dual big cell has J_3 F composed with id_3 in W_3, it equals one fixed g in G(C) on the connected domain. Use determination of higher Taylor coefficients and analytic continuation.

items.name: Order-two rigidity for complex balls
items.statement: For the complex unit ball of dimension at least two, the identity-orbit differential condition of order two forces a local biholomorphism to be a restriction of a projective automorphism. The one-dimensional disk requires order three.

items.name: Local projective geometry theorem
items.statement: A locally biholomorphic map between connected open subsets of projective space of dimension at least two which sends local line segments to projective lines extends to a projective linear transformation, in the precise local form used in the ball argument.

items.name: Highest-weight tangent variety rigidity
items.statement: For an irreducible compact Hermitian symmetric space of rank at least two, a local biholomorphism preserving the indicated variety of minimal rational tangents is induced by a global automorphism. Acquire Ochiai/Hwang-Mok hypotheses and distinguish local germs from global automorphisms.

items.name: Order-one rigidity in irreducible higher rank
items.statement: On an irreducible domain of rank at least two, preserving the first identity-jet orbit forces the local map to arise from G(C), using the highest-weight tangent variety and its rigidity.

items.name: Rigidity order for products
items.statement: For a product domain, order two suffices if no factor is a disk, and order one if every irreducible factor has rank at least two; retain factor decomposition and possible permutations in the automorphism comparison. Otherwise retain the uniform order-three theorem.

items.statement: Using the weighted compactification, compactified group action and proper analytic projection, show the saturation Y=G(C) D_k^r is constructible analytic in the nondegenerate jet product. Track boundary strata of the action correspondence.

items.name: Closedness of the jet saturation
items.statement: For k>=2, free G action and jet-disc automorphism transitivity on nondegenerate input jets make the saturation equidimensional in each projection. A hypothetical boundary has second-projection fibres of dimension below dim G but is G-invariant; freeness rules it out. Prove the symmetry and dimension statements before applying this argument.

items.name: Zariski closure of the jet graph
items.statement: The closed analytic saturation G(C) D_k^r is definable via its fundamental-set restriction, hence algebraic, and equals the Zariski closure of D_k^r by arithmetic Zariski density and invariance. Its fibres over the second jet factor have dimension dim G.

items.name: Transcendence degree of modular functions and derivatives
items.statement: In N+-translation coordinates z_1,...,z_n, the field generated over C by a finite set of function-field generators phi_i and their partial derivatives through order k>=2 has transcendence degree dim G. Adjoining C(z) leaves this relative transcendence degree dim G; the joint field has degree dim G+n over C.
items.note: The printed proof line trdeg_C C(z_1,...,z_n)=dim G is inconsistent for general n; the derivative field is the intended object. This interpretation and the finite-basis wording require independent review.

items.name: Higher modular derivatives are rational in order-two data
items.statement: The function field generated by all modular derivatives is generated by derivatives of orders at most two. Use the birational identification between the appropriate G-orbit spaces in characteristic zero; a bijective map of points alone does not establish an everywhere-regular inverse.

items.statement: The descended jet large-fibre incidence image is algebraic by proper analytic projection and definability, exactly with fixed order k separated from threshold d.

items.name: Normality of the generic stabilizer for jet families
items.statement: Apply the descended Hilbert-family monodromy argument to the jet setting, using the base projection and finite-index monodromy comparison. The connected algebraic stabilizer is normal in G.

items.name: Jet factor induction forces trivial connected stabilizer
items.statement: Split off the normal Theta factor, compare G-orbits and fibre dimensions of the jet projection, and use induction on domain dimension/defect to deduce Theta triviality for a minimal jet counterexample.

items.name: Jet translate induction and positive-dimensional stabilizer
items.statement: Adapt the volume/counting argument to the base projections of a minimal jet counterexample, also inducting on parameter count and analytic dimension so that purely vertical jet directions are handled. Obtain an infinite arithmetic stabilizer contradicting the trivial connected closure.
items.note: The phrase same proof as Lemma 4.3 does not by itself supply the vertical-rank reduction; this is an explicit remaining proof adapter.

items.name: Ax-Schanuel with derivatives in jet spaces
items.statement: For k>=2,r>=n, let W be irreducible algebraic in J_k^(nd,r) OmegaHat times J_k^(nd,r) X, restricted to Omega on the first base. Construct the Hilbert incidence, monodromy normality adapter, normal-factor induction and arithmetic translate argument as separate obligations. Then prove Theorem 9.1 for k>=2,r>=dim X with threshold dim U+dim G and nondegenerate formal jets; algebraize their G-saturation and prove Corollaries 9.3 and 10.4 with ambient derivatives. Construct rational/constructible Schwarzian charts and their equations. Extend the existing derivations to finite commuting families, Taylor prolongations and the precise Seidenberg realization. Resolve the full chain-rule compatibility of Theorem 11.3 before using its finite equations to define uniformized tuples in Theorem 12.1; then prove the trdeg lower bound rank(z)+dim G and the product version with exception in X^ell. Treat section 12.4 as an alternative implication, preserving formal coefficient rank versus base-image rank and avoiding a dependency cycle.
